author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I am not signing off on the production drift monitoring pipeline unless it carries full formal governance. A manual review process is not a substitute for reliable signal, especially during promotion weeks when a silent failure means empty shelves or unsold pallets. I refuse to accept a setup where we are flying blind on model degradation. If the checks do not have strict sign off and documented approval, I will not deploy them to the live environment. I need the assurance that every alert is reviewed by a designated owner before any automated action is taken. Without that structure, the risk of censored demand going unnoticed is too high for me to accept.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly refuses to sign off or deploy the pipeline without strict governance and designated owner review, establishing a non-negotiable line whose crossing constitutes refusal.
